$comment: INTEGRIQ DRAFT (native-data-gathering-provider, ported from spectr/connectors): Source and Job ship isEnabled false, per the requirement that a connector blocked on an unbuilt capability ships disabled. GAP: an N+1 two-hop fetch (an id list, then one detail request per id). Follow-up: the 'N+1 two-hop' change listed in native-data-gathering-provider tasks.md (Wave 2), not opened yet. Enable only once that change lands. ORIGINAL SPECTR NOTE: Phase-2 wave-2 OpenConnector ingestion config for Italy ANAC (Autorita Nazionale Anticorruzione OCDS API, api.anticorruzione.it/opendata/ocds/api/v1/1.0.0). Mirrors concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_italy_anac.py. Public, unauthenticated (keyless - docstring: 'No authentication required'). SHIPPED AS A DOCUMENTED DRAFT, Source + Job DISABLED, because of a genuine engine-shape blocker that neither oc#105 nor any current OpenConnector capability addresses: ANAC exposes NO bulk/list-of-releases endpoint. The real feed is a TWO-HOP N+1 fan-out - (1) GET /tender/ids returns a bare list of {"value": <id>} stubs (ids only, no tender content), then (2) the script fetches /releases/tender/{id} ONCE PER ID to get each actual OCDS release. OpenConnector's declarative synchronize path is single-fetch-then-map: `resultsPosition` extracts a records array from ONE fetched page and maps each element; it has no mechanism to take each element of a fetched list and issue a follow-up per-element HTTP GET to a Twig-templated detail endpoint, then map THOSE responses. (The `followUps`/`data`-injection machinery drives whole additional synchronizations, not a per-row detail fetch within one.) So pointing a Source at /tender/ids would only ever ingest id-stubs (no title/buyer/value), and pointing it at /releases/tender/{id} needs one id per run supplied externally - neither is a usable unattended feed. The mapping below is authored against the real /releases/tender/{id} OCDS release shape (ocid, tender.description as title - ANAC has no separate title field, buyer.name, tender.tenderPeriod.startDate/endDate, tender.items[].classification.id, tender.value.amount, tender.procurementMethodDetails, tender.mainProcurementCategory - all confirmed field paths from the script) so it is READY THE DAY OpenConnector grows a list-then-detail (N+1 detail-fetch) sync mode; until then it lands 0 objects. Additional script-confirmed quirks that would matter even with a detail-fetch mode: ANAC responses are slow (3-60s/id, script sets a 90s timeout) and UUID-style / special-char ids consistently time out or return [] (the script skips them via looks_like_problematic_id()) - a naive per-id crawl would be both slow and partially failing. Awards live inline in awards[] (no fan-out to tenderAward, per the declarative one-source->one-target limit). Recommended interim path if Italy coverage is needed before an N+1 mode exists: an ETL-style loader in etl/ (walk the id list, fetch each release, bulk-create) - out of this batch's scope. TED v3 already carries Italy's above-threshold EU notices meanwhile.
